patient._comment: 'patient' is info about the patient: personal, clinical, vitals are shown on the patient card during the game; diagnosis is used for potential 'patient review' card.

clinical.quoteLong: The room won't stop spinning and I keep listing to one side when I try to walk. It came on all of a sudden this morning. It's 'just' dizziness, but it won't quit and I can't stay upright.
clinical.presentationShort: 72yo M ? sudden persistent vertigo, truncal unsteadiness, direction-changing nystagmus, and inability to walk without assistance.
clinical.presentationLong: 72-year-old male with sudden persistent spinning dizziness. He lists to one side, has marked truncal unsteadiness and direction-changing nystagmus, and cannot stand or walk without assistance.

diagnosis.disposition: Acute → stroke pathway, MRI (plain CT often misses posterior strokes), neurology; 'just vertigo' can be a stroke.
diagnosis.why: Can't walk = central. Posterior strokes masquerade as 'vertigo' and CT misses them — think HINTS exam / MRI.
diagnosis.redFlag: Sudden vertigo + inability to walk / truncal ataxia = central (stroke), not benign peripheral vertigo.

answer._comment: 'answer' is answer for the game scoring.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: gripping the arm of the chair for balance, tilted to one side
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 72-year-old man who looks queasy, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: gripping the arm of the chair for balance, body tilted to one side. Expression: nauseated and off-balance. Clearly visible: a white-knuckle grip on the chair and an unsteady, tilted posture. No text, no logos.
